title: Ship the fantasy name list inside the app and load it automatically
description: Player access links are built from four professional players' surnames drawn from the tennis_players table, which migration 006 creates empty and which is filled only by running cmd/import-tennis-players against a JSON file. On a new instance the admin 'generate link' action therefore has nothing to draw from. Embed the committed tennis_players.json in the binary and load it at startup when the table is empty.
acceptance_criteria: On an empty database the tennis_players table is populated at startup from the embedded list, once
An already-populated table is left untouched
Generating a player link works on a brand-new instance with no CLI step
The load is logged with a count and failure to load is a clear startup error

notes: Token design (guessable by design, small-writes-only blast radius) is an accepted decision - do not change the token format here.

testing_requirements: Unit test: empty table gets seeded, non-empty table does not

context.user_story: As a new club administrator, I want player links to work straight away.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.
